explanation: The right hand is used for eating and handling food in Egypt, while the left is reserved for less clean, personal tasks — a distinction most sources trace to Islamic practice that is widely observed, including by many non-Muslim Egyptians in mixed settings. Directly putting food into your mouth with the left hand is seen as unhygienic and can cause offense.
local_tip: Eat and pass food with your right hand, and if you're left-handed, make a deliberate effort to switch at the table.

also_check.note: The left hand is reserved for toilet hygiene, so eating or passing food with it is considered unclean.
There is no stigma around which hand you use; chopstick technique matters far more.
There is no cultural taboo against eating with the left hand.

sources.title: Why Left-Handed Eating Is Frowned Upon In The Middle East
